entries.prompt: Produce ONE isolated detached Viking Predator biomask/helmet cutout, copied faithfully from the TWO supplied official Predator: Hunting Grounds images. This is a source-view production candidate, not an invented Norse helmet or a claimed canonical reconstruction. MAIN CAMERA: keep the exact slight three-quarter angle and slight downward pitch of the FIRST image, viking-render.png; the face points slightly toward image right. The SECOND official screenshot is only to check visible color placement and asymmetric details, not to turn the object into a frontal pose. Preserve the original mask outline, proportions, foreplate topology, engraved ornamental shapes and colors: dark blue-black metal upper dome with the large round decorated forehead medallion and concentric engraved bands; long paired upward curved horn structures with golden outer mounting plates and gray ridged tips; small subordinate points already visible near their roots; the broad worn silver lower face shell; the long golden engraved central nose plate with wider rounded lower end; a golden engraved eye-cover over the eye at IMAGE LEFT (wearer's anatomical right) and the dark open eye aperture at IMAGE RIGHT. Keep that asymmetry. Match source horn curvature, spacing and relative height, no extra horns. Keep the shallow gold brow bands and original asymmetric eye-cover outline. Small ornament detail should remain visually subordinate, no new runes or design additions. These source pictures establish visible coloration and shape, not hidden rear geometry. Remove the entire wearer: no black hanging dreadlocks, hair, exposed flesh, shoulders, armor, collar, necklaces, body, hands or skull trophy. In particular the large BLUE AXE BLADE and handle extending behind/above the head in the first picture are a WEAPON, not helmet parts: OMIT THE AXE COMPLETELY. Preserve just the true metal helmet, faceplate, horns and their attachments. No generic human Viking helmet, no hollow human nose guard, no additional eye, no beard. Match the game's realistic worn metal/shading as seen, with restrained neutral lighting preserving silver/gold/blue-black source colors. Do not redesign, mirror or symmetrize the face. Entire whole helmet including both horn tips fully inside a square 1254x1254 canvas, centered and sized about 75 percent of canvas height, at least 10 percent completely empty transparent alpha margin on all sides. Native transparent background, opaque metal core and clean antialiased silhouette. No checkerboard painting, no floor or cast shadow, no glow, scenery, text, watermark, frame, UI, duplicate objects or alternate views.

agentVisualAssessment.nativeBrowserAlphaReview: Independent reviewer compared v1 and v2 on black, white and checkerboard using native browser alpha. Both had clean contours; suspected white blobs in view_image were mostly alpha1–9/255 and did not establish a compositing defect. Version1 retained because version2 offered no visible alpha benefit and recomputed ornamental detail.
